gatherings.title: Gatherings & Events
gatherings.lede: What's coming up, how gatherings work, where we land, and the memory of past calls.
gatherings.whatBody: If you have never been, you may wonder what happens. Activities change from one gathering to the next. What tends to return is a fluid, diverse queer space where people of many ages, races, bodies, sexualities, genders, and beliefs come together — liberating for some, unfamiliar for others. If you are new, you can chat with an organiser first. If your heart is already saying yes, listen to that.
gatherings.coBody: Faeries say: if you see something that needs doing, the best way is to do it. A team helps beforehand; the event itself happens because of who comes. People chip in — meals, dishes, wood, workshops, heart circles, entertainment, sweeping up. Nothing particular is obligatory; participation is the gathering.
gatherings.lifeBody: We eat together — vegetarian with vegan options, cooked in the kitchen by whoever wants to help. Heart circles often run freer of city time-pressure and can open profound sharing. Workshops and activities may include ritual, dancing, drumming, theatre, music, art, games, fancy dress, silence, solitude, chaos, and more. If you bring it, it will most likely happen.
gatherings.careBody: A gathering aims to be inclusive, safe, and supporting. Organisers may speak with people when behaviour causes conflict, and may ask someone to leave to protect the whole. It is not group counselling — you hold responsibility for your own personal, emotional, physical, and sexual safety. Heart circles, understanding faeries, hugs, and organisers are around with support and love.
gatherings.payBody: Bank details are shared after booking; cash at the gathering is fine too. We hold NOTAFLOF close — No One Turned Away For Lack Of Funds. Gatherings are non-profit; additional donations are gratefully received.
gatherings.placesIntro: Castles, farms, lodges, and quieter land Circles return to. Tap a hearth for travel, bedding, access, and what to expect.
gatherings.featherBody: Near Haltwhistle and Hadrian's Wall — log fires, shared feasts, heart circles, dancing, drumming, and a drag room.
gatherings.featherExpectBody: A collaborative, co-created gathering — cook, chop wood, hold workshops, keep the castle cared for. The drag room offers a new outfit for every adventure.
gatherings.featherPractical1: Vegetarian and vegan meals. The castle can be cold — bring warm layers, slippers, outdoor clothes, boots, and a torch. Bring your own bedding and pillowcase; beds and mattresses are plentiful.
gatherings.featherPractical2: Baths and showers with hot water — bring towels. Fancy dress welcome in the drag room. Auctions often help fund the gathering.
gatherings.featherAccess: Ground floor is wheelchair accessible; dining and most social spaces are upstairs by stairs.
gatherings.featherAddress: Featherstone Castle, Hall Bank, Northumberland NE49 0JG — outside Haltwhistle, near Hadrian’s Wall.
gatherings.featherAir: By air: Newcastle, then train to Haltwhistle.
gatherings.featherTrain: Train via Carlisle or Newcastle to Haltwhistle — book early.
gatherings.featherCar: By car: three miles south-west of Haltwhistle on the A69.
gatherings.featherArrive: Arrive from noon on the first day; leave by noon on the last.
gatherings.glastoBody: A 43-acre organic farm at the foot of the Tor — long-house kitchens, house beds, and camping when the weather softens.
gatherings.glastoExpect1: A 43-acre organic farm at the foot of Glastonbury Tor. Gatherings are co-created — a core team holds the call and food; once we arrive, every contribution is welcome.
gatherings.glastoExpect2: Heart circles, shared vegan/vegetarian meals in the long-house kitchen, and daily tasks. If you see something that needs doing, why not be the one to do it?
gatherings.glastoPractical1: Rooms across several buildings; some uneven paths. Camping in warmer weather. Tell us access needs in advance. House beds usually include duvet, pillow, and bedding.
gatherings.glastoPractical2: Bring fancy dress for the drag room if you like, auction gifts, wellies, slippers, wet-weather gear, and note dietary needs on the booking form.
gatherings.glastoArrive: Arrive after 4pm on the first day; leave by 11am on departure day.
gatherings.glastoAddress: Paddington Farm Trust, Maidencroft Lane, Glastonbury BA6 8JN — about 30 minutes’ walk from town.
gatherings.glastoTrain: Train: London Paddington to Bristol or Taunton, then bus onward.
gatherings.glastoBus: Bus: Berrys to Glastonbury; National Express / Megabus to Bristol then local bus.
gatherings.glastoDriveShort: By car: approach from the west via Brindham Lane (///steady.rezoning.spurted).
gatherings.laughtonBody: Near Lewes on the edge of the South Downs — meadows, woodland, a sprung-floor hall, kitchen, guest rooms, and a fire-pit patio.
gatherings.laughtonExpect1: Laughton Lodge is a residential community on the edge of the South Downs, near Lewes — about 15 minutes from Lewes and 30 from Brighton. Albion Faeries gathered here for Lughnasadh, landing among meadows, woodland, gardens, and shared outdoor space.
gatherings.laughtonExpect2: The Shawfield event spaces include a large sprung-floor hall, professional kitchen, dining room, music room, guest rooms, and a patio with a fire pit — a southern hearth for ritual, feast, drumming, and rest under summer skies.
gatherings.laughtonPractical: Expect a rural community setting with indoor gathering rooms and outdoor land to roam. Bring layers for cool evenings, outdoor footwear, and whatever helps you settle into a co-created summer gathering. Exact bedding and capacity notes live with each gathering’s call when it opens.
gatherings.laughtonAddress: Laughton Lodge, Common Lane, Lewes, BN8 6BY — roughly 6 miles from Lewes, 15 from Brighton, and about 90 minutes from central London. Nearest stations: Lewes and Uckfield. Free parking on site.
gatherings.pardshawBody: Near Cockermouth in the Lake District. Communal sleeping across meeting rooms, wood stove, limited camping in the burial ground, no wifi. Intimate capacity — about 20 indoors and 5 camping.
gatherings.anybodyBody: A smaller rural barn venue used for focused co-created gatherings outside the usual festival calendar.
gatherings.sussexBody: Basic camping on a private estate recommended by faeries who gathered there — private, natural, and quieter than castle bookings when numbers need a different scale.
gatherings.balcombeBody: A southern camping / residential hearth used for summer Sussex gatherings.

gatherings.bridwellBody: Not an Albion-owned venue — festival land where Albion Faeries join the wider queer spiritual web for play, ritual, and camp.

who.title: Who we are
who.lede: An ever-expanding collective in the global Faerie web — spirit, sexuality, and chosen community across Albion.
who.todayBody: The Faeries of Albion are an ever-expanding collective network of lesbians, gay men, trans*, bisexuals, queer hetero people and anyone else in between, who come together to create vibrant, energetic and safe spaces to celebrate the spirituality in our sexuality; to develop our skills as healers, shamans and ritual workers; and as drummers, storytellers, performers, poets and artists, as well as community organisers, activists, and chefs.
who.heartBody: We appreciate and celebrate nature by communing with her spirits through play and ritual and explore a profound love for each other and the world through coming together in heart circle — a way of opening to one another sensitively and supporting any revelation or experience, with unconditional love.
who.spiritBody: We are proud to be part of the expansion of gay/queer life into the realms of the heart and spirit; to promote self awareness, expression and growth; and to be part of the renewal of Albion as a magical island where the wonders of spirit manifest.
who.webBody: The Albion Faeries are part of the global faerie web, connecting awakening, nature-loving, compassionate queers the world over.
who.faeriesP1: The Faeries are gay men and women plus men and women who prefer to use any other moniker that might describe them plus people that choose not to be called men or women plus beings who choose not to be called people. Faeries are organized as a group attempting to create community out of ritual and cooperation, except for faeries who are attempting to create community out of subversion of process and structure, as well as some faeries who wish to create chaos, often celebrating it, often not admitting it.
who.faeriesP2: Many faeries are spiritual, lifting whole or part of their spirituality from any one of the world’s religions or spiritualities. Some make up their own. Some make a mix. Some react against spirituality and religion as its own evil, some find a spiritual path in reacting against spirituality.
who.faeriesP3: Some Faeries just want to dress up in drag and perform in the woods, some want to dress up and not perform, some faeries want to dress up anywhere they can, some faeries don’t dress particularly different than they would in any other environment.
who.faeriesP4: Some faeries combine their spirituality with sex, some don’t, some are part of the faeries just to get laid. Some resent that. Some just want to drum by a camp-fire, and some want to camp far away from the drumming and get some sleep.
who.faeriesP5: This is what faeries are, except for faeries for which none of this applies.
who.circlesBody: Day-to-day work runs through Core Circles anyone may join: Finance, Communications, and Gatherings & Events. We aim for open, transparent meetings; major decisions go through Circles or Faessemblies. Convenors keep Circles meeting; Record-keepers keep minutes, archives, and follow-through alive. Roles are service, ideally pledged for about a year, with elder and neophyte backups where we can.
who.heartCircleBody: A Radical Faerie tradition for open, honest, loving communication. People meet in sacred space to speak from the heart and be listened to from the heart — with confidentiality, “I” statements, no debate or interruption, and a talisman that holds each person's turn. No one has to speak. It is not formal therapy, yet witnessing and being witnessed can be deeply healing.

involve.title: Get involved
involve.lede: We are an informal network of connected individuals. Come to a circle or gathering, join the mailing list, or find us on Faenet and Facebook.
involve.comeBody: Start with Gatherings & Events. No application form — arrive with care. If you are new to Faerie or queer space, you can write first and ask.
involve.newsBody: Gathering calls, booking openings, and other events. Sign up on the Albion Faeries newsletter list.
involve.connectBody: Faenet is a private Faerie social space. The Facebook group Radical Faerie UK has regional links and gathering chat.
involve.contactBody: General questions: faerieuk@gmail.com. Circle invites and organising: info@albionfaeries.org.uk. Prefer a form to a named Circle? Use the contact paths Circles already know — Comms, Finance, Gatherings & Events, Diversity & Inclusivity, or newsletter items.
involve.donateBody: Albion Faeries are entirely volunteer-run and not for profit. Donations sustain NOTAFLOF — helping people reach gatherings who might not otherwise — and cover small costs such as hosting.
involve.donateBank: Co-operative Bank · Account name Faerie UK · Sort code 08-92-99 · Account 65488214 · Reference Donation
involve.donateNote: One-off or regular gifts by bank transfer are preferred; PayPal is also used on the legacy site.
involve.circleBody: For faeries who already hold Circle work — notes, actions, and templates behind a quiet threshold.
involve.circlesHowIntro: Albion Faeries do not seek to be bound by strict policies, but to share and grow values, ethics, and principles together in mutual love and respect. Meetings and decisions aim to be as open and transparent as possible — with no formal membership, and an invitation to those who identify as part of the Radical Faeries of Albion.
involve.circlesHow1: Not everyone can be present at everything; a public mail-out keeps people in the loop.
involve.circlesHow2: Hosts of private meeting spaces may say who receives their address.
involve.circlesHow3: Working parties handle focused detail; Faessemblies are open potentially to all radical faeries.
involve.circlesHow4: Faessembly and Core Circle meetings should be advertised with due notice. Major decisions go through Core Circles or Faessemblies — working groups are not empowered to decide for the whole community.
involve.circlesHow5: Large residential gatherings include a general assembly; Stewards aim for these at least twice a year in different parts of Albion.
involve.circlesMapCaption: From the open Faessembly hearth, care gathers in the Stewards Circle, then flows through three Core Circles - with working parties rooting the practical work.
involve.circlesCoreIntro: Day-to-day work runs through three Core Circles. Any Albion Faerie may attend if they wish to help.
involve.circlesCoreFinance: Finance — oversees matters relating to finance.
involve.circlesCoreComms: Communications — oversees matters relating to communication.
involve.circlesCoreEvents: Gatherings & Events — oversees how gatherings and events are organised.
involve.circlesRolesIntro: Roles relate to tasks undertaken as service. A twelve-month pledge is usually requested; roles may be shared. Major roles are asked to find two backups — an elder with experience and a neophyte learning into the work. Convenors, Record-keepers, and local or specialist stewards come together as the Stewards Circle.
involve.circlesConvenorsBody: Keep each Core Circle meeting regularly, encourage attendance, arrange accessible venues, spot who can lead issues, support facilitators, and keep an overview with other Stewards.
involve.circlesRecordsBody: Support Convenors; publicise meetings; ensure minutes are taken, circulated, stored, and followed through; encourage skill-sharing; and co-ordinate with other Stewards. The three Convenors and three Record-keepers also liaise across Circles.
involve.circlesVolunteersBody: Facilitators and minute-takers are essential and can serve occasionally. Circles may appoint working-party leaders and specialist stewards — for example a Book-Keeper — who pledge particular skills. Local stewards are still developing wherever enough faeries live nearby.

lugh.title: Gathering call
lugh.tag: Template hearth for an Albion gathering — the call, practicals, and how to help.
lugh.callBody: Calling Radical Faeries, Queer Spirits, Gay Witches, Drag Druids, heart circlers, fae newbies, and whoever else you may be — welcome home. Exact dates and place live under Gatherings & Events and in the newsletter when bookings open.
lugh.practicalBody: Travel, beds or camping, what to bring, access notes, and care agreements belong on each gathering's own page — Featherstone, Glastonbury, or elsewhere.
lugh.helpBody: Kitchens, stewards, ritual holders, and drivers make the gathering. Offer what you can; if you want to help plan, write to Gatherings & Events.
